summary: A browser where AI agents like Claude Code or Codex do web tasks in their own isolated spaces while you keep browsing.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: ego lite is a browser built for working alongside AI agents. Each agent runs its browser tasks in its own Space, an isolated workspace inside the same browser, so it never takes over your tabs. Agents connect through the ego-browser skill, which works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or a custom agent CLI and exposes page snapshots and actions like fill and click as JavaScript tools. On first launch it can import your Chrome data so agents can use your existing logins. This repository holds the skill and docs under MIT; the browser app is a separate free download.
sixtySeconds.problem: Browser automation tools usually drive a separate browser, lose your logins, or fight you for control. ego lite gives agents their own space in a browser you also use.
whoFor: People using Claude Code, Codex or Cursor for web tasks
Developers running parallel scraping or research jobs
Users who want agents to use their own logins
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it when you want agents to work in a real browser with your sessions, in parallel, without interrupting your own browsing.
requirements: macOS or Windows (Linux is on the roadmap)
An agent CLI such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor

overview: Download the ego lite app, or add the ego-browser skill with npx skills add citrolabs/ego-lite and let your agent walk you through installing the app.
On first launch, choose whether to migrate your Chrome data, which lets agents use your logins, cookies and extensions.
In your agent CLI, type /ego-browser and describe a task in plain language.

tutorial.title: Run your first agent browser task
setup: An agent CLI such as Claude Code

steps.title: Start the skill
steps.body: In your agent CLI, type /ego-browser followed by a space.

steps.title: Describe the task
steps.body: Write what you want in plain language, such as reading a page and summarizing it.

steps.title: Watch it work
steps.body: The agent opens the page in its own Space, reads a snapshot, acts, and reports back while your tabs stay untouched.

tutorial.expected: The agent completes the task in its own Space and reports the result.
